title: What If You Ate an Airplane? One Man Did, and It Took Two Years

scenes.text: What if you tried to eat an airplane? Guinness says one man finished the whole thing.
In 1978, French performer Michel Lotito started on a Cessna 150, sawn into bite-sized pieces.
He swallowed them like pills, about two pounds of metal a day, washed down with mineral oil and a lot of water.
By 1980, two years later, the plane was gone.
Doctors X-rayed him. He was said to have an unusually thick stomach lining, but his blood tests looked like anyone else's.
Guinness estimates he ate about nine tons of metal in his life. Bananas and boiled eggs? Those gave him heartburn.

description:
What if you tried to eat an airplane? Guinness World Records says the French entertainer Michel Lotito, known as Monsieur Mangetout, ate a whole Cessna 150 between 1978 and 1980.
He cut objects into small pieces with a power saw and swallowed them with mineral oil and plenty of water, up to about 900 grams of metal a day; Guinness also lists 18 bicycles, 15 supermarket trolleys and a coffin, roughly nine tons in all, and gave him its strangest diet record. Doctors described a thick stomach and intestinal lining but never found a full medical explanation, and the fact-checker Snopes could not independently confirm the aircraft. Swallowing metal is dangerous and nobody should copy it.

first_comment: Guinness gave him a brass plaque for the record. He ate that too. What is your what-if about the human body?
